title: Claims status regression
inputDescription: fixtures/workload.json: 60 status requests from one customer (CUS-000123), 10 ms apart (0 to 590 ms), replayed through observe() of the revision under test. The starting revision is the released starter (a4d88ab), where references/good.mjs keeps the 30-second per-customer cache and references/broken.mjs is the regression that removed it. The good revision makes 1 upstream call; the broken one makes 60 within 590 ms.

checks.condition: The observation is an object with non-empty requests, arrays upstreamCalls/responses/logs, well-formed {customerCode, atMs} entries, string log lines and a requirements object with positive maxRequestsPerSecond and cacheTtlMs and non-empty forbiddenLogFragments. Otherwise it fails with MALFORMED, because none of the requirements can be judged.

Grouping upstreamCalls by customerCode and ordering each group by atMs, every consecutive pair is at least requirements.cacheTtlMs (30000 ms) apart. A refresh exactly 30000 ms later passes; different customers are judged independently.
For every rolling window [t, t + 1000 ms) over upstreamCalls (not incoming requests), the number of calls is at most requirements.maxRequestsPerSecond (50). 50 calls in one second pass; 51 fail.
No string in logs contains any entry of requirements.forbiddenLogFragments (case-insensitive substring). Any other log text passes, so refactors may change harmless log wording.
